title: Gotrade Daily: US Markets Closed, Friday Ends Early
summary: US markets are closed for Thanksgiving and open for a half day on Friday. Here is Wednesday's recap and the stocks to watch for Friday's session.
body_markdown:
### Nvidia, Deere and HP


**Nvidia ([NVDA](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/nvda/) )** fell after S&P Global placed Nvidia's AA issuer credit rating on CreditWatch Negative. The agency cited management and governance risks, including board independence and "key man" risk, according to CNBC. Nvidia shares are down 27% in November.


**Deere & Company ([DE](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/de/) )** reported fourth-quarter net income of $1.051 billion, or $3.89 per share, compared with $3.93 a year earlier. For fiscal 2027, Deere forecast net income of $4.50 billion to $5.25 billion, according to the[company's release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/315189/000110465926131741/de-ex99d1.htm) .


**HP Inc. ([HPQ](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/hpq/) )** reported fourth-quarter net revenue of $16.0 billion, up 9.3%, and raised its quarterly dividend to $0.31 per share, according to the[company's release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/47217/000004721726000054/hp103126exhibit991q426.htm) .


### Black Friday in focus


Adobe forecasts US online spending of $6.9 billion on Thanksgiving and $12.9 billion on Black Friday, up 9.2% from last year, according to[Adobe's forecast](https://news.adobe.com/news/2026/09/adobe-us-holiday-shopping-season-to-hit-record) released in September. Retail stocks such as **Amazon ([AMZN](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/amzn/) )** are in focus as shopping data starts to come in.


## Pre-Market Pulse 📊


There is no regular session tonight. On Wednesday, the Nasdaq fell 3.3% just after the open before recovering. CNBC linked the rebound to light trading ahead of the holiday and a blog post by Michael Burry saying his portfolio was temporarily almost entirely long.


## Macro Note 📝


The PCE data reinforced expectations of Federal Reserve rate hikes in December and January,[according to CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/24/stock-market-today-live-updates-.html) .


## Conclusion


Wednesday showed a market that is still fragile, with indexes falling sharply and then recovering within one session. Inflation data, the tariff proposal and Nvidia news still hang over Friday's short session, and Black Friday shopping data is the next thing to watch.
